search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; transcript-complexity-corrected reusable validation; post-selection e-values; max-information; behavior-equivalent complexity; fresh-audit tradeoffs

public_sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
public_sources.authors: Cynthia Dwork; Vitaly Feldman; Moritz Hardt; Toniann Pitassi; Omer Reingold; Aaron Roth
public_sources.used_scope: Description-length correction for adaptive data reuse: if an adaptive transcript has a finite range Y, a bad-event probability beta for each fixed transcript inflates by at most |Y| via a union bound. Also supplies approximate max-information as a unifying information measure.

public_sources.title: Max-Information, Differential Privacy, and Post-Selection Hypothesis Testing
public_sources.authors: Ryan Rogers; Aaron Roth; Adam Smith; Om Thakkar
public_sources.used_scope: For a data-dependent selector with beta-approximate max-information k bits, any bad-event probability under independent selection is inflated to at most 2^k times that probability plus beta. The paper gives post-selection p-value correction and warns that approximate-DP-derived product-distribution max-information does not compose safely in arbitrary order.

public_sources.title: What Fits (Into Few Tokens) Doesn't Overfit: Compression and Generalization in ML Research Agents
public_sources.authors: Martin Andres Bertran; Aaron Roth; Zhiwei Steven Wu
public_sources.used_scope: A concrete agentic one-bit ladder where the j-th improvement checkpoint has at most C(T_max-1,j-1) validation-dependent transcripts. With T_max=50, K_max=7, the final checkpoint has about 14 million transcripts. The guarantee depends on the validation channel being the only data-dependent channel.

public_sources.title: Family-wise Error Rate Control with E-values
public_sources.used_scope: E-value closed testing can give strong FWER control and, with e-processes, always-valid sequential FWER control. Used as support that valid fixed-hypothesis e-processes can be combined into stronger multiplicity procedures after the adaptive-data validity problem has been corrected.

public_sources.title: PAC-Bayes Beyond Parameter Space: Behavioral Equivalence, Z-Information, and Exact Complexity Decomposition
public_sources.authors: Vasant G. Honavar; Satish Kumar Keshri; Neil Ashtekar; Zehao Liu
public_sources.used_scope: Predictive risk depends on predictive behavior rather than the internal realization; PAC-Bayes complexity decomposes into behavior-selection and within-behavior realization terms. Used only to motivate exact behavior-level quotienting of transcript complexity, not as a theorem about e-value selection.

prefix_weighted_anytime_reuse_certificat.setup: Before observing validation data D, fix a countable index set U of all counterfactual test opportunities (for example full validation-feedback transcript plus attempt identifier), a prior mass pi_u with sum_u pi_u <= 1, and a decoder Phi that maps each u plus training data and validation-independent randomness to a fixed candidate h_u. For each u construct an e-process E_{u,t} valid for H_u when h_u is fixed. Candidate generation may adapt arbitrarily to D only through the declared index/transcript u.
prefix_weighted_anytime_reuse_certificat.rule: For the actually selected opportunity U(D), commit only if its fixed-hypothesis e-process crosses 1/(alpha*pi_U). Equivalently, with prefix-code length L(U) and pi_U=2^{-L(U)}, require raw e-wealth >= 2^{L(U)}/alpha.
prefix_weighted_anytime_reuse_certificat.strong_error_statement: For any set of true-null opportunities, P(any false commit ever) <= sum_{u true null} P(sup_t E_{u,t} >= 1/(alpha*pi_u)) <= alpha*sum pi_u <= alpha. No independence between opportunities is required. Repeated attempts must either share one cumulative valid process or be separately indexed and charged prior mass.
prefix_weighted_anytime_reuse_certificat.what_it_repairs: This turns the previous reused-dev failure into an explicit complexity payment. The candidate-level conditional sign null need not remain true after adaptive selection; instead each counterfactual candidate must have a valid fixed-candidate replay/e-process, and selection is paid for by prior mass.
prefix_weighted_anytime_reuse_certificat.implementation_requirement: After selection, evaluate the frozen candidate on a canonical validation replay/order whose fixed-candidate e-process is valid. The decoder must not read raw validation data except through the declared transcript. Every validation-dependent side channel that can influence the candidate or test opportunity must be encoded in u or hidden/padded.
prefix_weighted_anytime_reuse_certificat.scope_guard: This is a worker-local derivation from Ville/Markov plus weighted union over a predeclared counterfactual universe. It is not claimed to be a named theorem from the cited papers. If U or Phi is itself chosen using validation data without paying for that choice, the guarantee fails.

max_information_to_anytime_e_correction.setup: Let A(D) select one candidate/test opportunity and suppose beta-approximate max-information I_inf^beta(D;A(D)) <= k bits. For every fixed selected value a that is null, assume a fixed-candidate e-process with P(sup_t E_{a,t} >= c) <= 1/c.
max_information_to_anytime_e_correction.derivation: Under an independent coupling D tensor A(D), the false-commit event has probability <=1/c. The max-information event inequality then gives actual probability <= 2^k/c + beta. Therefore choose c = 2^k/(alpha-beta) for alpha>beta.
max_information_to_anytime_e_correction.interpretation: Literal B-bit description-length correction is the k approximately B worst-case special case. A tighter independently justified max-information bound can be materially cheaper than charging the full transcript range.
max_information_to_anytime_e_correction.scope_guard: The DP-to-max-information route in Rogers et al. for approximate DP requires product-distributed input and has an adaptive-composition order caveat. Do not insert an approximate-DP mechanism after earlier data-dependent conditioning and assume the same k bound automatically composes.

behavior_quotient_prior.mechanism: If multiple transcript/implementation indices provably decode to exactly the same test-relevant predictive behavior, aggregate their predeclared masses into Pi_behavior=sum pi_u and test one behavior-level e-process at threshold 1/(alpha*Pi_behavior).
behavior_quotient_prior.benefit: Avoids paying repeatedly for syntactic paths or internal realizations that are prediction-equivalent; aligns the complexity object with behavior rather than implementation multiplicity.
behavior_quotient_prior.scope_guard: Equivalence must be fixed independently of validation and preserve the relevant outcome distribution, not merely agree on the reused validation sample. Approximate or empirical equivalence needs a separate error term/theorem.

worked_attack_correction.prior_attack: Previous checkpoint's memorizer corrects exactly 8 selected dev failures and obtains default PACE wealth 1.5^8=25.62890625, enough to cross the naive alpha=.05 threshold 20 while population gain is zero in the nonatomic construction.

if_transcript_names_8_of_40.result: The dev memorizer no longer certifies.

worked_attack_correction.scope_guard: These ladder thresholds apply the worker-local weighted-e/Ville derivation to the paper's transcript counts; the paper itself reports generalization confidence intervals, not these e-process thresholds.

power_cost_simulation.simulation: 250000 Monte Carlo alternative trajectories; fixed sign bet q_bet=.75; true discordant sign win probability=.75; task discordance probability=.4; alpha=.05. Complexity B bits multiplies the raw e threshold by 2^B. Separate 500000-trajectory null sanity check used q=.5.
power_cost_simulation.interpretation: Even 5-10 bits of validation-dependent candidate selection can dominate the sample cost at 10-50 task horizons. Fresh confirmation is often far cheaper unless the reused-validation transcript is extremely compressed or a tighter prior/max-information bound is available.
power_cost_simulation.scope_guard: Simulation is worker-local and only checks this stylized Bernoulli/discordance model; empirical null crossing is not a proof.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Make every validation-dependent candidate/test opportunity a member of a predeclared counterfactual universe with prior mass pi; replay a valid fixed-candidate e-process and require E >= 1/(alpha*pi). This yields strong anytime false-commit control by weighted Ville plus union, despite arbitrary adaptive selection through the declared transcript.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local derivation grounded in description-length adaptive-data analysis and standard e-process/FWER theory; stress-tested against the prior memorization counterexample and finite-horizon simulations.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Requires a fixed decoder/universe and complete accounting of validation-dependent side channels. Can be prohibitively conservative when transcript complexity is more than a few bits.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: If the selector's approximate max-information is bounded by k bits with failure beta, raise the selected fixed-candidate anytime threshold from 1/alpha to 2^k/(alpha-beta).
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct worker-local conversion of Rogers et al.'s max-information bad-event inequality using Ville's fixed-candidate crossing probability as the independent-selection bad event.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Needs a valid k,beta bound for the full validation-dependent selector. Approximate-DP-derived bounds have product-distribution and composition-order caveats.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Aggregate prior mass over exactly behavior-equivalent transcript/implementation paths before charging adaptive-selection complexity.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local weighted-union quotient plus 2026 PAC-Bayes behavior-space decomposition showing that predictive behavior is the risk-relevant object rather than realization multiplicity.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Only exact, validation-independent equivalence is currently justified; approximate equivalence remains open.

measurement_validity_rules.rule_1: For reused-validation commit gates, distinguish fixed-candidate evidence validity from candidate-selection validity. A valid fixed-candidate e-process can be made selection-safe by charging the full counterfactual selection information.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_2: A prefix/description code must count all validation-dependent observables that can alter the candidate or test opportunity: feedback bits, stop time, score bins, exception/latency shape, item identities, and any visible evidence trajectory unless mechanically hidden or padded.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_3: Do not call pi_M*sup_t E_{M,t} itself an e-value. The rigorous guarantee used here is a weighted Ville crossing rule plus union over fixed counterfactual tests.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_4: If repeated attempts restart evidence, encode the attempt identity and pay new prior mass; alternatively maintain one valid cumulative process for that fixed null.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_5: When a literal transcript correction costs more than a fresh audit, prefer fresh audit unless a tighter predeclared prior, behavior quotient, or independently proved max-information bound materially lowers the penalty.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_6: DP/privacy of an e-value and DP/stability of the validation-feedback selector solve different problems. Do not conflate private hypothesis testing with adaptive-data generalization.

rejected_overgeneralizations: Anytime-valid fixed-candidate e-values are automatically valid after arbitrary reused-dev candidate selection.
One-bit feedback means only one bit of total selection complexity regardless of the number and locations of feedback events.
A candidate reached by many syntactically different transcripts must necessarily pay each path separately even when exact behavior equivalence is proved in advance.
Approximate differential privacy can be inserted at any point of an already adaptively conditioned validation loop and automatically yields the same product-distribution max-information guarantee.
The worker-local weighted transcript correction is power-competitive with fresh audit at small task horizons; simulations show it can be dramatically more expensive.

frontier_queue.action: Derive a nonuniform prior/code for realistic self-evolution transcripts (prefix code over improvement locations, stop time, candidate family and bounded metadata) and optimize expected complexity under a validation-independent deployment prior. Compare against uniform transcript counting and fresh-audit blocks.

Investigate whether e-value closed testing/e-FWER machinery can recover power after prefix-weighted candidate-validity correction when multiple behavior-level candidates share a structured tree, while retaining strong anytime false-commit control under arbitrary dependence.

Search for direct approximate-max-information or privacy-loss accounting tailored to low-information agent feedback transcripts that yields k substantially below literal worst-case description length, with explicit composition order and side-channel accounting.

Extend behavior quotienting from exact predictive equivalence to approximate equivalence with an explicit slack term in the e-process/null, and determine whether near-duplicate candidate paths can be safely compressed.

Simulate full adaptive proposal loops rather than independent candidate abstractions: compare naive reused PACE, prefix-weighted replay, max-info-corrected replay, and fresh audit on false commits, power, total validation items, and information returned to the proposer.

exact_next_action: Construct and optimize a realistic prefix prior over low-information self-evolution transcripts, including stop-time and metadata side channels, then quantify when its weighted-anytime certificate beats or loses to fresh audit under 10-200 independent tasks.
